newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. reports progress in Afghan peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. reports progress in Afghan peace talks.

text.p: The United Nations said on Wednesday a series of meetings between representatives of the warring Afghan factions over the last three days had reached a concrete and practical agreement on several key points.

"Although the Working Group did not enjoy decision-making power, it reached concrete and practical agreement on several key points," said the statement from the U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan (UNSMA).

"These included the urgency of an immediate ceasefire in Afghanistan and the need to view this ceasefire as a first and major step toward a lasting political process and dialogue rather than as an end in itself," it said.

Representatives of the purist Islamic Taleban movement and the alliance opposing it had five, two-hour meetings over three days under the chairmanship of Norbert Holl, the U.N. special representative to Afghanistan, in the Pakistani capital Islamabad.
"The meeting ... discussed a number of key issues of peace in Afghanistan," the statement said.

It listed the issues as the implementation of an immediate and nationwide ceasefire, establishment of a commission to supervise and monitor the ceasefire, demilitarisation of Kabul, exchange of prisoners, and "creation of suitable conditions for the establishment of a broad-based and fully representative government".

The participants were not empowered to make commitments on behalf of their factions, and the meetings were designed to find common ground and produce a framework the representatives could take back to their leaderships for further consultation.
A UNSMA member, Steven Evans, told Reuters that the meeting had been held in a friendly atmosphere and that the mission was happy with the outcome.
"We are well pleased with the outcome and atmosphere," he said.
"The meeting of the working group was held in a constructive and brotherly atmosphere, characterised by a free and frank exchange of views," the UNSMA statement said.
It said the participants had agreed to meet again next month to continue their discussions and that UNSMA representatives would also consult the faction leaders to speed up the process.

The working group consisted of three memers each from the Taleban (Mullah Wakhil Ahmed, Masoom Afghani and Abdul Wahab) and the opposition alliance (General Payenda, Mohammed Ishaq and Mohammed Rasool Taleb).

The Taleban, who control about two-thirds of Afghanistan, are facing the forces of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and his allies on frontlines some 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul and in the remote northwestern provinces.
